findings.title: topics#unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: In the new `unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — for example a user who received a notification email for a topic they have never opened or been tracked on (invited-to-topic, invited-to-PM, or watched-category emails where no topic_users row exists yet). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError on nil and returning a 500 to anyone who clicks the new email unsubscribe link in that situation. The code must handle a missing record (e.g. create one via TopicUser.change) before reading the level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET request, enabling cross-site request forgery
findings.body: The new routes `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` mutate the logged-in user's topic notification level via GET. Rails' CSRF protection only covers non-GET requests, so any third-party page can embed `` and silently change notification levels (muting topics, or downgrading watching/tracking to regular) for every logged-in user who views it. State changes like this should be made resistant to cross-site GETs (e.g. require a POST/PUT with an authenticity token, or a per-user token in the URL as done for email unsubscribe keys).

findings.title: unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id is not set and auto-track can silently undo the unsubscribe
findings.body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. TopicUser.change is what normally sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id = user_changed` when the level changes. Because those columns are left untouched here, any topic_users row whose `notifications_reason_id` is still null (records created by track_visit!/update_last_read) will have its level automatically bumped back to `tracking` by the auto-track logic in `TopicUser.update_last_read` the next time the user reads the topic — silently re-subscribing the user after they explicitly unsubscribed. The direct save also skips the MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish that other clients rely on.

findings.title: Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking any email built with add_unsubscribe_link but without that option
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared `unsubscribe_link` string to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` (line 90) and `#html_part` (line 67) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and `unsubscribe_url` is only added to template_args if the caller passes it as an opt — MessageBuilder provides no default. Ruby I18n raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationData` for missing interpolation arguments, so any mailer (including plugins or future core mailers) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise instead of sending. The spec had to be amended to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to keep passing, which demonstrates the new hard requirement. MessageBuilder should default `unsubscribe_url` (or the translation should be split) so the option remains optional.

findings.title: No controller specs for the new topics#unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action implements non-trivial behavior — a 301 redirect when the slug is missing/mismatched, a notification-level toggle (watching/tracking → regular, otherwise → muted), and HTML/JSON responses via perform_show_response — but no request specs were added for it. Combined with the nil TopicUser crash and the GET-mutation concerns above, the action ships completely untested; at minimum there should be specs covering the redirect, each starting notification level, and the case where no topic_users record exists.

findings.title: Email/page copy promises notifications will stop, but the action only downgrades tracking/watching users to regular
findings.body: The new email footer text says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" and the unsubscribe page says "You will stop receiving notifications for ...". However, the toggle logic sets users at `tracking` or `watching` to `regular` (only `muted` truly stops notifications). At the `regular` level Discourse still sends notifications (e.g. replies to the user's own posts, PMs), so users who click the link believing they will receive nothing further will keep getting emails, which is both a UX trap and can push recipients toward marking the site's mail as spam. Either the copy should be softened or the action should set `muted` for all levels.
